clue.text: Forget beans turning mouldy in Hungarian dish

indicators.note: milk turning goes sour, and here the letters of the two words go bad and rearrange

parts.note: food that has gone mouldy is off

explanation.surface: A cook warns against using beans that have gone mouldy in a goulash-style dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' shuffles the two words FORGET BEANS. The dish is usually thought of as Russian, so 'Hungarian' is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew of sliced beef in soured cream sauce, a classic Eastern European meat dish.

clue.text: Old, old bottles, in other words lacking spares

parts.note: EX is a former partner, so something old

indicators.note: lacking means the bottles word is without the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: used, drained bottles are empties
i.e. (id est) means in other words

explanation.surface: Someone describes old bottles, rephrasing it as having no spare parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' appears twice: the first is the former-partner abbreviation, the second belongs with 'bottles'. 'lacking' removes the abbreviation for 'in other words'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare someone a duty is to excuse or free them from it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Check filling for pesto panini

indicators.note: the answer sits as a filling inside the words pesto panini, like a sandwich filling

explanation.surface: Someone checks what goes inside a pesto sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: To check a movement is to halt it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Contemplative being in a field?

definitions.meaning: given to pondering, chewing things over
a creature grazing in a meadow, such as a cow or sheep that chews the cud

explanation.definitionFit: Cud-chewing grazers such as cattle and sheep; the adjective also means meditative or pondering.

clue.text: Baffled actor Wayne becomes batty here

parts.note: 'you've got me' means you've baffled me, so got stands for baffled
a ham is a poor overacting actor

explanation.surface: A puzzled film star named Wayne goes mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayne is Bruce Wayne, who turns into the Bat-man in his home city; John Wayne the actor is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional city where billionaire Bruce Wayne dons the bat costume to fight crime.

clue.text: Order ban on latex to be unlevied

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to prohibit latex, on the grounds that it escapes duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on which no levy or duty is charged is exempt from tax.

clue.text: Cool card representing devotional organisation

parts.note: a fan cools you down
a club is a playing card of the clubs suit

explanation.surface: A trendy playing card stands for a religious body.
explanation.definitionFit: A society of devoted admirers of a star or team; 'devotional' is wordplay on devotees.

clue.text: Religion is manacling misbehaving

indicators.note: letters that misbehave do not stay in line, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A faith accused of chaining people up and behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: The faith and practice of the Church of England, a Christian denomination.

clue.text: Devise new layout for tamer novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A designer reworks the pages of a book for a lion tamer.
explanation.definitionFit: To give text or a disk a fresh arrangement or format, a computing term.

clue.text: Sample of non-inflammable reversible silk fabric

indicators.note: a reversible garment can be turned round, so the sampled letters are read backwards
a sample is a small piece taken from the word non-inflammable

explanation.surface: A swatch of fireproof silk that can be worn either side out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sample of' takes NONIN from non-inflammable; 'reversible' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheer lightweight fabric of silk or chiffon, used for dresses and lingerie.

clue.text: Avoid lift in American truck

parts.note: to dodge is to avoid
a pick-up is a lift, collecting someone in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone escapes having to give a ride in a US lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodge is a US vehicle maker, and an open-backed light lorry is the make's light truck model.

clue.text: Sorry trail's end has been lost, backtracking

indicators.note: going back along a trail reads the letters backwards
the final letter of the trail word is gone

parts.note: spoor is the trail of an animal

explanation.surface: A tracker apologises after losing the end of the trail and turning back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end has been lost' cuts SPOOR to SPOO; 'backtracking' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of apology or dismay after a small mistake.

clue.text: Simultaneously going my way?

definitions.meaning: happening at the same time, as parallel processes do
lines running side by side travel in the same direction

explanation.definitionFit: Parallel tracks run alongside each other, so things done this way happen side by side or concurrently.

clue.text: Flimsy scenery, reportedly, for profitable screening?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the words are a sound-alike

parts.note: flimsy is thin paper, and scenery is a view, giving paper view

explanation.surface: A theatre critic sneers at cardboard sets made for a moneymaking show.
explanation.definitionFit: Television where viewers are charged for each programme watched, so the broadcast earns money.

clue.text: One gets power from these rabbit items on the menu

parts.note: rabbit and gas are both British slang for chatter
mains are main courses on a menu

explanation.surface: Rabbit dishes on a menu that give a diner energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground pipes that carry fuel supply to homes, giving energy for cooking and heating.

clue.text: One is writer with odd feet

parts.note: one is I, and I is ... becomes I am
a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: A self-introduction from an author who has misshapen feet.
explanation.walkthrough: In verse, a foot is a unit of rhythm; 'odd' hints that this one is lopsided, short then long.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse in this metre uses feet of one unstressed and one stressed syllable, unequal units.

clue.text: Wrongdoers chatter on board

indicators.note: being on a vessel means being carried inside it, so the chatter word goes within the ship letters

parts.note: to go on board is to go aboard ship, and SS (steamship) is the usual crossword ship
a chatter is a person who talks, a talker

explanation.surface: Criminals chat while sailing on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the convention for putting something inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: People who follow and harass others obsessively, offenders under the law.

clue.text: Tidies formal afterthought

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal
PS, a postscript, is an afterthought in a letter

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up a stiff letter, adding a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: To smarten one's appearance fussily, adjusting hair and clothes.

clue.text: Split where 19th-century humor can be found

definitions.meaning: split means divided into two parts
Mark Twain was the great American humorist of the 1800s, so his humor lies in his writings; the US spelling of humor is a hint

explanation.definitionFit: An old phrase meaning asunder or into two pieces, and literally 'in' the writer Mark Twain.

clue.text: Stan grabs Ollie carelessly losing back-end of pantomime horse

indicators.note: Stan grabbing something holds it inside his name
letters handled carelessly fall out of order
the name Ollie loses a letter
the back end of pantomime is its final letter

explanation.surface: Laurel and Hardy in a pantomime horse costume, Stan clutching Ollie, who carelessly drops the rear half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes E off OLLIE, and 'carelessly' rearranges the OLLI left into LLIO, which STAN 'grabs'.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse, especially one kept for breeding.

clue.text: Arrive at not so hot spot

parts.note: to infer is to arrive at a conclusion
'no' is the reply meaning 'not so', a denial

explanation.surface: A traveller reaches a place that is less hot than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so' looks like it qualifies 'hot'; it is the denial that gives NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A raging fire or hell, Dante's fiery underworld, is a very hot place.

clue.text: Stuff consumed in all quarters but west

indicators.note: in puts the eating word inside the compass points

parts.note: the compass points without W are S, E and N
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Food eaten everywhere except in the west.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff means cloth, and this is a glossy cotton cloth woven like satin.

clue.text: Cries: 'Supply food!' Sausages or ice cream perhaps to be delivered

parts.note: to cater is to provide food

indicators.note: words delivered are spoken, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: Wall's is a British brand known for sausages and ice cream

explanation.surface: A shout to a caterer to bring sausages or ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: Wall's is a long-standing British food brand that has made both sausages and ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrill howls like a cat's yowling, loud wails.

clue.text: What can be regularly spotted among buffoons?

definitions.text: What can be regularly spotted among buffoons?

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of buffoons

explanation.surface: Something seen often among fools.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of 'buffoons' gives the answer, and the whole clue jokes that cranks claim regular sightings.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects, which people report sighting in the sky.

clue.text: Pal wanting a bit of a jaw

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the pal word loses an a

parts.note: china is a pal in Cockney rhyming slang, from china plate = mate

explanation.surface: A friend who wants a bit of a chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' drops the A from CHINA. In Cockney rhyming slang, china plate rhymes with mate, so china means pal.
explanation.definitionFit: The front of the lower jaw, part of the jawbone.

clue.text: Yum, a mighty absorbing tastebud tickler

indicators.note: the words Yum, a mighty absorb and hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic diner praises a delicious mouthful.
explanation.definitionFit: The savoury fifth basic taste, as of broth or soy sauce.

clue.text: What Cliff could shout out in each of six decades — it's a record

indicators.note: shouting out is speaking, so the words are a sound-alike

parts.note: what Cliff Richard says of himself begins with the first person pronoun
Cliff Richard had a hit in the charts in each of six decades, so he could say he does chart

explanation.surface: Cliff Richard boasts of a chart run lasting six decades, a pop record.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard is a British pop singer with UK hit singles in every decade from the 1950s to the 2000s, a record.
explanation.definitionFit: The optician's board of letters, loosely a listing or record of letters of shrinking size.

clue.text: Differentiate between scallion and shallot to show familiarity with the subject

definitions.meaning: telling one bulb vegetable from another, literally recognising alliums
to be expert, to understand a topic thoroughly

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being expert in one's field, taken literally as identifying bulb vegetables.
